info.description:
Product information management API -------
Summary It is built top of Erply's current product database. Its goal is to allow user to: * Extend the dataset (ie., users can decide what fields a product can have, and can themselves define an arbitrary number of categorizations); * Get data in and out of the system easily (ie. an API must support imports and integrations); * Easily make large-scale updates (ie., recategorize items in bulk, make whole catalogs or groups active or inactive) * Support omni-channel organization (allow specifying which products should be available in which sales channels) * Enrich data (see which items have a certain property missing, fill missing fields) Product information management API is compatible with Erply's current data model, and the existing API calls
Auth with Cookies Add `apisession_` cookie with your session key + `clientCode` HTTP header
Bulk operations The bulk operations are processed concurrently, therefore the response items order is not the same as the request items one. Each bulk response item has its own identifier: **resultID**. The **resourceID** field refer to the REST resource being worker with.
Translatable names and descriptions Some entities have fields `name`, `description`, or both that are translatable. These fields support more languages than English. Make `getActiveLanguages` Erply API call to get a list of activated languages for your account. Use the `isoCode` field of the language to specify the language. For example , `en` for English, `fr` for French. For example to send a name in 3 languages, French, German and Dutch, the payload should be: ```json { "name": { "fr": "nom", "de": "name", "nl": "naam" } } ``` The same structure applies for 1. brand or product group description, in those cases instead of `"name"` it is `"description"`. 2. matrix dimension name, in that case instead of `"name"` it is `"dimension_name"`. 3. matrix dimension value name, in that case instead of `"name"` it is `"dimension_value_name"`. In case of a description ```json { "description": { "fr": { "html": "description", "plain_text": "description" }, "de": { "html": "bezeichnung", "plain_text": "bezeichnung" }, "nl": { "html": "omschrijving", "plain_text": "omschrijving" } } } ``` Not active languages would be accepted and not return an error in the response. But they are not guaranteed to be saved.
Response headers on every endpoint * **Request-Time-Unix** header contains server time in a format of unix timestamp.
Filtering & Sorting The filtering and sorting parameters provide flexibility to the user to accelerate user's performance and increase efficiency. ### Filtering: The 'filter' query parameter represents a JSON array of arrays of length 3 and a string. Each array represents a filter and the string - operand: **and**, **or**. For the array, 1st string is the field name, 2nd string is the operands, and the 3rd object is the value (can be any type). Supported operands: **=**, **!=**, **>=**, **<=**, **in**, **not in**, **contains** and **startswith**.
general filtering JSON example a filter to fetch actively sold burgers with groupID more than 2. >
> 

> [
>    [
>        "id",
>        "in",
>        [1, 2, 3]
>    ],
>    [
>        "group_id",
>        ">=",
>        "2"
>    ],
>    "and",
>    [
>        "status",
>        "!=",
>        "ACTIVE"
>    ],
>    "and",
>    [
>        "name.en",
>        "contains",
>        "burger"
>    ]
> ]
>
>
single filter JSON example The single filter must be still an array of arrays. For example a filter to fetch active records. >
> 

> [
>    [
>        "status",
>        "=",
>        "ACTIVE"
>    ]
> ]
>
>
nested filter JSON example The filters can also be nested to produce more complex searches. >
> 

> [
>    [
>       [
>           "status",
>           "=",
>           "ACTIVE"
>       ],
>       "and",
>       [
>           "group_id",
>           ">=",
>           "2"
>       ]
>    ],
>    "or",
>    [
>        "id",
>        "in",
>        [1, 2, 3]
>    ]
> ]
>
>
#### 'or' operand
filtering 'or' operand JSON example for example a filter to fetch matrix or bundle products: >
> 

> [
>   [
>       "type",
>       "=",
>       "MATRIX"
>   ],
>   "or",
>   [
>       "type",
>       "=",
>       "BUNDLE"
>   ]
> ]
>
>
In the previous example we have used the same classifier 'type' multiple times - in two filters. **NB!** Translatable classifiers such as name and description, etc **cannot be used** multiple times, For example you cannot lookup products that have english name 'apple' and/or greek name 'μήλο'. ### Sorting The sorting parameter is the 'sort' query parameter. It's a JSON object with 3 fields: 1. selector - field name, example value:added, 2. desc - short for descending, value: true or false, 3. language: example value: gr, is used to sort by translatable fields such as name.
sorting JSON example >
> 

> {
>    "selector": "added",
>    "desc": true,
>    "language": "gr"
> }
>
>
Backup & Restore With PIM API you can create a backup of the product catalogue and then restore it when needed. ### Creating a backup To **create a backup** you need to specify the **backup_id** field on the product when creating or updating it one by one or in bulk. It is allowed to have only one backup at a time. All new backups will override the previous ones. For example, if you created and updated some products specifying with backup_id equals 3, then the first **create or update** operation with the backup_id equals 7 will delete all the backups associated with the backup_id equals 3. ### Restoring To **restore** you should request the ```/product/restore``` endpoint with the **backup_id**.
------- **[Go SDK](https://github.com/erply/pim-go-wrapper)** - make the API requests from your Go service with comfort. -------

For type MAX_VALUE, input the maximum allowed value as a signed integer or decimal.

rule.description:
Rule "value" or whatever to call this: the numeric qualifier that goes hand in hand with that particular rule type. Eg. I specify that my parameter must have at least a minimum number of characters and that minimum number is 5.
For type REQUIRED, leave empty.
For type MIN_LENGTH, input the required minimum length as an integer.
For type MAX_LENGTH, input the required maximum length as an integer.
For type MIN_VALUE, input the minimum allowed value as a signed integer or decimal (eg. “0”, “-1”, “25.6”, “-9.999999” etc.)
For type MAX_VALUE, input the maximum allowed value as a signed integer or decimal.
For type INPUT_CASE, input 0 for "LOWERCASE" or 1 for “UPPERCASE”.
For type PRECISION, input the number of allowed decimal places as an integer (eg. “0”, “1”, or “2”)
